facts.fact: Enclosed attics and enclosed rafter spaces need a total net free ventilating area of at least 1/150 of the area of the vented space. It may be reduced to 1/300 only when 40-50% of the required vent area is in the upper part of the attic (no more than 3 ft below the ridge) and, in Climate Zones 6-8, a Class I or II vapor retarder is installed on the warm-in-winter side of the ceiling.
Each end of a ceiling joist or rafter must have at least 1-1/2 in of bearing on wood or metal and at least 3 in of bearing on masonry or concrete.
A handrail mounted next to a wall or other surface must have a clear space of at least 1-1/2 in between the handrail and the wall.
Each wood shingle or wood shake must be attached with two fasteners, which must be corrosion resistant.

Where a gravel or crushed-stone foundation drain is required, the drainage material must extend at least 12 in beyond the outside edge of the footing and its top must be at least 6 in above the top of the footing.
When no soil investigation is done, the presumptive allowable bearing pressure for clay, sandy clay, silty clay, clayey silt and silt (CL, ML, MH, CH) is 1,500 psf.

Presumptive allowable foundation pressures: crystalline bedrock 12,000 psf; sedimentary and foliated rock 4,000 psf; sandy gravel and gravel (GW, GP) 3,000 psf; sand, silty or clayey sand and silty or clayey gravel 2,000 psf; clays and silts 1,500 psf.
Commercial kitchens use an occupant load factor of 200 gross sq ft per occupant. A 42 ft x 70 ft kitchen (2,940 sq ft) works out to 14.7, which is rounded up to 15 occupants.
facts.note: Card answers 14, which truncates 14.7. Fractional occupant loads are rounded up in design practice (ICC commentary), giving 15. The 200 gross factor itself is correct.

facts.fact: For resilient channels on a stud wall, the bottom channel is placed about 2 in above the floor and the top channel within 6 in of the ceiling.
facts.note: Manufacturer handbook guidance (USG); not a code requirement and may vary by edition or product.

facts.fact: When old plaster and lath are removed for a conventional plaster job, 3/8 in gypsum lath (Rocklath) is the recommended plaster base.
facts.note: Product-specific manufacturer recommendation; cannot confirm against a code.

facts.fact: A door frame that extends to the ceiling can act as a vertical control joint in a gypsum board partition.
facts.note: Manufacturer handbook guidance; not a code rule.

facts.fact: Veneer plaster drying (setting) time depends mainly on air temperature, relative humidity and air movement across the surface.
Conditions around 80 degrees F and 65% relative humidity fall within the normal drying range for veneer plaster finishes.
facts.note: Manufacturer handbook drying chart; values cannot be independently confirmed.

facts.source: USG Gypsum Construction Handbook (joint compound coverage)
facts.fact: About 9.4 gallons of ready-mixed lightweight all-purpose joint compound are estimated to finish 1,000 sq ft of gypsum board.
facts.note: Product-specific coverage figure from a manufacturer handbook; varies by product and finish level.

facts.fact: Conventional-weight all-purpose joint compound is sanded with fine paper, roughly 120 grit or finer, to avoid scuffing the board face.
facts.note: Manufacturer recommendations on grit differ by product (some say 150 or finer); cannot confirm the exact grit.

facts.fact: An oxygen-deficient atmosphere contains less than 19.5% oxygen by volume; an oxygen-enriched atmosphere contains more than 23.5%.
A temporary radiant-type room heater must have at least 36 in of clearance to combustible material at its sides.

An anchorage for personal fall arrest must support at least 5,000 lb per employee attached, or be designed, installed and used under a qualified person's supervision as part of a complete system with a safety factor of at least two.
facts.note: Card says 5,400 lb dead weight, which comes from the old 29 CFR 1926.104 lifeline rule. Current personal fall arrest anchorage strength is 5,000 lb per attached employee under 1926.502(d)(15).

facts.fact: Driveways between and around outdoor combustible storage piles must be at least 15 ft wide, kept clear, and spaced so no grid unit exceeds 50 ft by 150 ft.
Outdoor piles of combustible materials must be stable and may never be stacked higher than 20 ft.
In open yard storage areas, portable fire extinguishers rated at least 2A must be placed so the travel distance to the nearest one does not exceed 100 ft.
A stairway or ladder must be provided at every point of worker access where there is a break in elevation of 19 in or more, unless a ramp, runway, embankment or personnel hoist is provided.

A competent person must inspect excavations, adjacent areas and protective systems daily before work starts and as needed during the shift, and again after every rainstorm or other event that increases the hazard.
Repointing (tuckpointing) mortar should be prehydrated before use and is usually a Type N or softer mortar so it is not stronger than the original masonry.
Grout mixed with more water than specified can segregate (aggregate separates from the paste) and shrink excessively in the cells.
Abrasive blasting of brick is done at low to moderate nozzle pressure, roughly 60-100 psi, to avoid damaging the brick face and mortar joints.
facts.note: Card gives 60-100 'psf', an obvious unit error for psi. Recommended pressures vary by source and abrasive; cannot confirm the exact range.

facts.source: TMS 402 composite wall ties (referenced by IBC 2021 Ch. 21)
facts.fact: In composite masonry walls, wire wall ties may be spaced no more than 36 in apart horizontally and 24 in apart vertically.
A shear wall is a wall designed to resist lateral forces (wind or seismic) acting parallel to the plane of the wall.
Passive attic ventilation uses natural airflow: air enters through soffit or eave vents and exits through ridge vents, with no fans.
Wet-spray cellulose insulation must dry to a low moisture content (often cited as below about 19%) before drywall is installed over it.
facts.note: Manufacturer limits vary (some allow up to 25%); the 19% figure cannot be confirmed as a single standard.

facts.fact: Dry dimension lumber is smaller than its nominal size: a 2x4 is 1-1/2 x 3-1/2 in, 2x6 is 1-1/2 x 5-1/2 in, 2x8 is 1-1/2 x 7-1/4 in, 2x10 is 1-1/2 x 9-1/4 in and 2x12 is 1-1/2 x 11-1/4 in.
Unseasoned (green) 2x6 lumber is dressed to 1-9/16 x 5-5/8 in, so it is 3/8 in narrower than a 6 in steel stud.
The raised ribs (deformations) on reinforcing bars are made on purpose to improve bond, so the concrete grips the steel and load transfers between them.
Copper water tube is color coded by wall thickness: Type K (thickest) green, Type L blue, Type M (thinnest) red.
For a straight partition, studs = (length in inches / spacing) + 1; a 12 ft wall at 16 in on center needs 144/16 + 1 = 10 studs before adding for corners, openings or waste.
A pocket door frame must be installed during framing, before the drywall, because the door slides into a cavity inside the wall.
When excavated, blasted rock swells the most (roughly 50-65% from bank to loose volume), more than clay, loam or sand, so it needs the most haul capacity per bank cubic yard.
Trench volume = average width x depth x length. A trench 18 ft wide at the top, 5 ft wide at the bottom, 8 ft deep and 750 ft long holds (18+5)/2 x 8 x 750 = 69,000 cu ft (about 2,556 cu yd).
facts.note: Card states an 18-inch top width but answers 69,000 cu ft, which only works with an 18-ft top width; with 18 in the volume would be 19,500 cu ft.

facts.fact: Framing for a fixed-glass curtain wall must be rigid enough to carry lateral wind loads on the glass without excessive deflection.
Connections in precast concrete frames are usually treated as pinned, so they resist little moment; lateral stability must come from shear walls, bracing or other lateral systems.
facts.note: Card says pin-type connections provide lateral stability. Pinned connections do not resist moment, so stability has to be provided by a separate lateral system.

facts.fact: A topographic survey shows existing ground contours and elevations; the sitework contractor compares it to design grades to figure cut and fill.
Loam shrinks when compacted relative to its bank volume; one textbook shrinkage factor given for loam is about 0.83.
facts.note: Shrinkage and load factors vary by reference table (common values for loam range about 0.80-0.90); cannot confirm 0.83 as standard.

facts.fact: Walls, partitions and floor-ceiling assemblies separating dwelling or sleeping units from each other or from public areas must have an STC of at least 50 (45 if field tested); floor-ceiling assemblies also need an IIC of at least 50 (45 field tested).

facts.source: NASCLA Contractor's Guide topic: employee handbooks
facts.fact: Company employee handbooks cover policies for current employees (pay, conduct, benefits, safety); hiring practices are generally kept out of the employee manual.
facts.note: From a multiple-choice card with no options shown; cannot confirm this is a firm rule.

facts.source: NASCLA Contractor's Guide topic: labor burden
facts.fact: True labor cost includes more than wages: the employer's payroll taxes (FICA, FUTA, SUTA), workers' compensation insurance and fringe benefits are part of the labor burden.

Under the FLSA, work an employer suffers or permits is paid work time, so unauthorized overtime by a non-exempt employee must still be paid at the overtime rate; the employer may discipline the employee but cannot withhold the pay.

Programmed OSHA inspections are planned inspections aimed at high-hazard industries or establishments with high injury and illness rates; unprogrammed inspections respond to imminent danger, fatalities, complaints and referrals.

facts.source: National Environmental Policy Act, 42 USC 4321 et seq.
facts.fact: NEPA applies to major federal actions, such as projects that are federally funded, federally permitted or on federal land, and requires their environmental effects to be evaluated.
The best way to limit VOC exposure is to choose low-VOC (low-emitting) products and to store VOC-containing materials in a well-ventilated area sealed off from occupied spaces.

Before any demolition or renovation, the affected part of the building must be thoroughly inspected for asbestos (by an accredited inspector), and the regulating agency must be notified at least 10 working days before demolition or a regulated renovation begins.

facts.source: TSCA Section 16; 40 CFR Part 19 (civil penalty inflation adjustments)
facts.fact: Violating EPA lead-based paint rules (such as the RRP rule) can bring civil penalties per violation per day; the cap started at $37,500 and is raised each year for inflation, now exceeding $48,000.
facts.note: Card says up to $37,500 per day, the original 2008-era amount. EPA adjusts TSCA penalties annually for inflation and the current maximum is well above that.

facts.fact: Lead abatement means measures designed to permanently eliminate lead-based paint hazards, unlike interim controls, which reduce hazards temporarily.
An emergency action plan must be written, kept at the workplace and available to employees when the employer has more than 10 employees; with 10 or fewer it may be communicated orally.

Medicare tax is 1.45% of all wages for the employee and another 1.45% for the employer, and the employer must withhold an extra 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on an employee's wages above $200,000 in a year (employee only). Social Security tax is 6.2% each, up to the annual wage base.
Fixed assets are long-term tangible assets used to run the business, such as equipment, vehicles, buildings and land, and they are depreciated (except land).
Owner's equity is the owner's stake in the business: what the owner invested plus retained earnings, equal to total assets minus total liabilities.
Gross profit equals revenue minus cost of goods sold (for a contractor, direct construction costs); net profit then subtracts overhead and other expenses.
A profitable sole proprietor has no employer withholding on business income, so they avoid the underpayment penalty by making quarterly estimated tax payments (Form 1040-ES).

Federal payroll tax deposits must be made by electronic funds transfer, usually through EFTPS; paper deposit coupons (Form 8109) were discontinued after 2010. An employer with less than $2,500 of liability for the quarter may instead pay with a timely filed Form 941.
facts.note: Card says corporations may mail deposits with a payment coupon. The IRS eliminated Form 8109 deposit coupons as of January 1, 2011; deposits must be made electronically.

facts.fact: Employers must withhold federal income tax and the employee's share of FICA (Social Security and Medicare) from paychecks; FUTA is paid only by the employer and is never withheld.
Net income divided by revenue is the net profit margin, a profitability ratio showing how much of each sales dollar is kept as profit.

An employer whose total employment taxes in the lookback period were $50,000 or less deposits monthly; more than $50,000 means semiweekly deposits, and a $100,000 liability on any day must be deposited the next business day.
The main drawback of cash-basis accounting is that revenue and expenses are recorded when cash moves, so expenses may not be matched to the revenue they produced in the same period.

facts.source: IRS guidance: Do you need an EIN?
facts.fact: A sole proprietor or single-member LLC may use the owner's SSN instead of an EIN only if it has no employees and does not file excise, employment or pension plan returns; once it hires employees it needs an EIN.
facts.note: Card says sole proprietors and single-owner LLCs do not need an EIN, without the condition. They need one as soon as they have employees or certain filing obligations.

facts.fact: Failure-to-deposit penalties: 2% for deposits 1-5 days late, 5% for 6-15 days late, 10% for more than 15 days late, and 15% if still unpaid 10 days after the first IRS notice.
If accumulated FUTA tax exceeds $500 at the end of a quarter, it must be deposited by the last day of the month after that quarter; the Form 940 return itself is filed once a year, due January 31.
facts.note: Card says unemployment tax over $500 must be filed quarterly. The deposit is quarterly; the FUTA return (Form 940) is filed annually.

facts.source: Contract law fundamentals; statute of frauds
facts.fact: Oral contracts can be binding but are discouraged because their terms are hard to prove in a dispute, and some contracts (e.g. real estate or those not performable within a year) must be in writing under the statute of frauds.

On federal construction contracts covered by the Miller Act, the payment bond must equal 100% of the original contract price unless the contracting officer finds that impractical, so a $5.1 million contract needs a $5.1 million payment bond.
facts.note: Cards claim $2.5 million on a $5.1M contract and 40% ($1,040,000) on a $2.6M contract. Those are the pre-1999 tiered amounts; the 1999 amendments set the payment bond at 100% of contract value.

facts.fact: A bid bond assures the owner that the bidder bid in good faith and, if awarded, will sign the contract and provide the required performance and payment bonds; otherwise the surety pays damages up to the bond amount.
A valid contract is an agreement between two or more parties with legal capacity, with offer and acceptance (mutual assent), consideration and a lawful purpose.
Under AIA-based contracts, the architect reviews the contractor's application for payment and certifies to the owner the amount due based on work completed before a progress payment is made.

facts.source: AIA A201 Article 7 (changes in the work)
facts.fact: A change order is a written instrument, signed by owner, contractor and architect, that adds to, deletes from or alters the contract work and may adjust the contract sum and contract time.

facts.source: IRS General Instructions for Information Returns (1099-NEC, 1099-MISC)
facts.fact: Recipient copies of Form 1099-NEC (used since tax year 2020 for nonemployee compensation paid to subcontractors) and most Form 1099-MISC must be furnished by January 31.

The small-contractor exception that allows the completed-contract method (instead of percentage of completion) applies to contracts expected to finish within 2 years by contractors whose average annual gross receipts for the prior 3 years do not exceed the inflation-indexed limit ($25 million base; $31 million for tax years beginning in 2025).
facts.note: Card says $10 million, the pre-2018 limit. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act raised it to $25 million indexed for inflation.

facts.fact: The Miller Act, enacted in 1935, requires performance and payment bonds on federal construction contracts (currently those over $150,000 under the FAR), because liens cannot be filed against federal property.
On federal construction projects, the performance bond is normally 100% of the original contract price.
In mediation a neutral helps the parties reach their own voluntary settlement; in arbitration a neutral third party hears the case and issues a decision that is usually binding on the parties.

facts.source: IRS guidance: Do you need a new EIN?
facts.fact: A new owner who buys an existing business generally must get a new EIN; the seller's EIN cannot simply be taken over.
A flow-down clause binds the subcontractor to the general contractor the same way the general contractor is bound to the owner under the prime contract.
A three-phase panel has three ungrounded (hot) phase legs, A, B and C; a three-phase four-wire service adds a grounded neutral conductor to those three phases.

Sillcocks, hose bibbs, wall hydrants and other hose connections must have backflow protection from an atmospheric-type or pressure-type vacuum breaker or a permanently attached hose-connection vacuum breaker.

Neutral (grounded) conductors and equipment grounding conductors are bonded together only at the service disconnect; in a subpanel downstream of the service they must be kept on separate, isolated bars.

Maximum horizontal pipe support spacing includes: PVC and ABS 4 ft; CPVC 1 in and smaller 3 ft; PEX 1 in and smaller 32 in; copper tubing 1-1/4 in and smaller 6 ft; cast iron 5 ft (10 ft with 10 ft lengths); steel 12 ft.
facts.note: Card says PVC needs the most horizontal support. PVC (4 ft) needs closer support than metal pipe, but PEX and polybutylene (32 in) and small CPVC (3 ft) need even closer support.

facts.fact: Rebar can be a grounding electrode: at least 20 ft of 1/2 in or larger bar in a footing in contact with earth, encased in at least 2 in of concrete (a concrete-encased or Ufer electrode). Metal underground gas piping and aluminum may not be used as grounding electrodes.
facts.note: Card says rebar cannot be used for grounding. The NEC expressly permits concrete-encased rebar electrodes; gas piping and aluminum are the prohibited ones.

facts.fact: Underground cables under a building normally must be in a raceway, but Type MC cable listed for direct burial (and MI cable embedded in concrete or fill) may run under a building without a raceway.
facts.note: Exception added in the 2017 NEC; whether it applies depends on the NEC edition the jurisdiction has adopted.

facts.fact: A kitchen sink needs a 1-1/2 in trap, including when it serves a food waste disposer and dishwasher.

facts.source: Clean Water Act NPDES; EPA Construction General Permit
facts.fact: A federal NPDES stormwater permit is required for construction that disturbs 1 acre or more, or less than 1 acre if part of a larger common plan of development that disturbs 1 acre or more.

For construction more than 8 ft tall, pedestrian protection depends on setback from the lot line: under 5 ft needs a barrier and covered walkway, 5 ft up to 1/4 the height needs a barrier and covered walkway, 1/4 to 1/2 the height needs a barrier, and more than 1/2 the height needs none. A 48 ft building set back 20 ft (between 12 and 24 ft) needs a barrier.
A door in the means of egress, when fully open, may not reduce the required egress width by more than 7 in, and at any position it may not reduce the required width by more than half.

Retaining walls no more than 4 ft high, measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, are exempt from a permit unless they support a surcharge or impound Class I, II or IIIA liquids.

Steel joist placement plans must show loads, nonstandard joist profiles, support and splice connections, deflection criteria, bridging size and location, and joist headers, but they do not need the seal and signature of the joist manufacturer's registered design professional.
An enclosed fire service access elevator lobby must be at least 150 sq ft with no dimension less than 8 ft.
Where ramp handrails are not continuous between runs, they must extend horizontally at least 12 in beyond the top and bottom of each ramp run.
Spray-applied fireproofing on steel generally requires ambient and substrate temperatures of at least 40 degrees F during application and for about 24 hours after.
facts.note: Temperature limits come from product manufacturers, not the IBC; values vary by product.

facts.fact: Pedestrians must be protected by directional barricades where a walkway in front of a construction site extends into the street; such walkways must be at least 4 ft wide.
Floor members are limited to a live-load deflection of L/360 (span divided by 360); the IBC limit for total dead plus live load on floors is L/240.
Footings must be stepped where the bottom of the footing slopes more than 1 vertical in 10 horizontal (10%).
Door thresholds may be no more than 3/4 in high for sliding doors serving dwelling units and no more than 1/2 in high for other doors.

Notches at the ends of solid lumber joists may not exceed 1/4 of the joist depth; notches elsewhere are limited to 1/6 of the depth, no longer than 1/3 of the depth, and not in the middle third of the span.

Drip edge on shingle roofs must be mechanically fastened at no more than 12 in on center, overlap adjacent pieces at least 2 in, extend at least 1/4 in below the sheathing, and extend at least 2 in back onto the deck.
On shingle roofs, drip edge goes under the underlayment at eaves and over the underlayment along rake edges.

Where fire-protective covering on a structural member could be damaged by vehicles, material handling or similar activity, it must be protected by corner guards or a metal or noncombustible jacket at least 5 ft above the finished floor.

Asphalt shingles must be attached with corrosion-resistant roofing nails (galvanized steel, stainless steel, aluminum or copper) with at least a 12-gauge shank and a 3/8 in head; staples are not an approved fastener.

Fire protection systems must pass acceptance tests witnessed by the fire code official, and it is unlawful to occupy a structure until the required detection, alarm and suppression systems have been tested and approved.

Buildings with fire service access elevators must be fully sprinklered, except that sprinklers may not be installed in the machine rooms, machinery spaces, control rooms, control spaces or hoistways of those elevators.
A masonry chimney must extend at least 3 ft above the highest point where it passes through the roof and at least 2 ft higher than any part of the building within 10 ft.

Extinguisher cabinets generally may not be locked, but in Group I-3 occupancies and mental health areas of Group I-2 occupancies, extinguishers may be locked up or kept at staff locations if staff have keys.

Any story or basement over 1,500 sq ft must be sprinklered unless it has qualifying exterior openings for fire department access, and each such opening must have a minimum dimension of at least 30 in.

Exterior wood siding, sheathing and wall framing less than 6 in above the ground, or less than 2 in above concrete steps, porches, patios or similar exposed surfaces, must be naturally durable or preservative-treated wood.

In high-rise buildings 420 ft or less in height, fire barriers around vertical shafts (other than interior exit stairways and elevator hoistways) may be reduced to a 1-hour rating if automatic sprinklers are installed in the shafts at the top and at alternate floors.

Type I handrails with a circular cross section must be 1-1/4 to 2 in in outside diameter; non-circular Type I handrails must have a perimeter of 4 to 6-1/4 in and a cross section no larger than 2-1/4 in.
A clearance of at least 3 ft is required between automatic sprinklers and the top of piles of loose combustible fibers.
facts.note: Could not confirm the exact IFC section or value; general storage uses an 18 in clearance below sprinkler deflectors.

facts.fact: Fire separation distance is measured at right angles from the building face to the closest interior lot line, to the centerline of a street, alley or public way, or to an imaginary line between two buildings on the same lot.
Deep foundation elements standing unbraced in air, water or fluid soils may be considered laterally supported at a point 5 ft into stiff soil or 10 ft into soft soil unless otherwise approved.

When a fire-rated column extends through a ceiling, its fire protection must run continuously from the top of the foundation or floor/ceiling assembly below, through the ceiling space, to the top of the column.

Interior masonry chimneys (including where they pass through floors and roofs) need at least 2 in of air space clearance to combustibles; chimneys located entirely outside the exterior walls need at least 1 in.
Manual fire alarm boxes (pull stations) must be within 5 ft of the entrance to each exit, with the operable part 42 to 48 in above the floor.

Landings at doors must be at least as wide as the stairway or door, whichever is greater, and at least 44 in long in the direction of travel; in Group R-3, Group U and inside dwelling units the minimum length is 36 in.
Structural steel H-piles must have a nominal depth in the direction of the web of at least 8 in, flange and web thickness of at least 3/8 in, and flange width at least 80% of the section depth.

Once construction is more than 40 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access, a temporary or permanent stairway is required, extended as work progresses to within one floor of the highest point with secured decking or flooring.

For an embedded post or pole, the hole must be at least 4 in larger than the column's diameter at its bottom, or 4 in larger than the diagonal of a square or rectangular column, to leave room for backfill.
Stair risers must be vertical or sloped under the tread above at no more than 30 degrees from vertical, measured from the underside of the nosing above.
Means of egress illumination must be at least 1 footcandle (11 lux) at the walking surface whenever the building is occupied.
Cast-in-place or grouted-in-place deep foundation elements must have a diameter of at least 12 in without a permanent casing, or a nominal outside diameter of at least 8 in with a permanent casing.
The foundation or superstructure must be designed to handle a deep foundation element being out of position by at least 3 in.

Accessible car parking spaces must be at least 96 in wide with access aisles at least 60 in wide; where spaces and aisles are marked with lines, widths are measured from the centerline of the markings.
Objects with leading edges between 27 and 80 in above the floor may protrude no more than 4 in horizontally into a circulation path.
A door to a single-user toilet or bathing room may swing into the turning space if a clear floor space of at least 30 x 48 in is provided inside the room beyond the arc of the door swing.
In a private residence elevator, the clearance between the car platform and the edge of any landing sill may not exceed 1-1/4 in.
Accessible elevator car control buttons and hall call buttons must be at least 3/4 in in their smallest dimension.
Trusses are to be set close to their plan locations along the bearing; one cited tolerance is within 1/4 in of the dimension shown.
facts.note: Industry installation guide value; could not confirm the exact tolerance figure.

facts.fact: Lifting guidance for trusses depends on span: shorter trusses (around 30 ft) may be lifted at one or two pick points with taglines, while longer trusses need spreader bars and more pick points.
facts.note: Cards conflict (one says 1 pick point for parallel-chord trusses up to 30 ft, another says 2 points for 30 ft single trusses); exact counts depend on truss type in BCSI diagrams.

facts.fact: Temporary lateral restraint and bracing for trusses is attached to each truss with at least two 16d nails.
facts.note: Industry guide (BCSI) recommendation rather than code; nail specifications may vary by edition.

facts.fact: A rough estimate of wood truss weight is about 15 lb per linear foot, so a bundle of seven 32 ft trusses weighs roughly 7 x 32 x 15 = 3,360 lb.
facts.note: Rule-of-thumb figure; actual truss weight varies widely with depth, lumber and design.

facts.fact: The FAA must be notified at least 45 days ahead (Form 7460-1) for a crane or structure more than 200 ft above ground, or one that would penetrate a 100:1 slope within 20,000 ft (about 3.8 mi) of a public-use airport runway longer than 3,200 ft (50:1 within 10,000 ft for shorter runways, 25:1 within 5,000 ft of a heliport).
facts.note: Card says 5 miles. FAA notice under 14 CFR 77.9 is based on height and imaginary-surface slopes within 20,000 ft, 10,000 ft or 5,000 ft depending on the facility, not a 5-mile radius.

facts.fact: Prestressed members are unloaded in their upright (as-cast service) orientation and lifted and supported at points near their ends unless other points are designated.
facts.note: From precast industry (PCI) handling guidance; cannot confirm exact wording against the source.

facts.fact: When stacking stemmed members or hollow-core plank, dunnage should not run continuously across more than one stack of precast units.
facts.note: Precast industry storage guidance; cannot confirm against the source document.

facts.fact: Drypack is mortar mixed with just enough water to make a stiff, damp, crumbly material that is rammed or packed into place, often under base plates or in voids.

In a two-leg bridle, each leg carries (load / 2) / sin(angle from horizontal). At 45 degrees each leg carries about 0.707 times the total load, so a 50,000 lb lift puts about 35,400 lb on each leg; size the rope from the rated-capacity tables.

questions.q: Without using any reduction allowed by the code, the net free ventilating area of an enclosed attic must be at least what fraction of the vented space?
questions.why: The base requirement is 1/150; 1/300 is allowed only when high/low vent split and vapor retarder conditions are met.

questions.q: What is the minimum bearing length for the end of a ceiling joist resting on a wood top plate?
questions.why: Joists and rafters need 1-1/2 in of bearing on wood or metal; 3 in is required on masonry or concrete.

questions.q: With no soil investigation, what presumptive allowable bearing pressure may be used for silty clay?
questions.why: Clays and silts (CL, ML, MH, CH) carry a presumptive value of 1,500 psf.

questions.q: What presumptive allowable foundation pressure applies to sandy gravel (GW or GP)?
questions.why: Sandy gravel and gravel are assigned 3,000 psf; 4,000 is for sedimentary rock and 12,000 for crystalline bedrock.

questions.q: Which occupant load factor does the IBC assign to a commercial kitchen?
questions.why: Commercial kitchens are figured at 200 gross sq ft per occupant, with fractional results rounded up.

questions.q: Below what oxygen concentration is an atmosphere considered oxygen deficient?
questions.why: Less than 19.5% oxygen is deficient; more than 23.5% is enriched. Normal air is about 20.9%.

questions.q: Unless designed by a qualified person with a safety factor of two, an anchorage for personal fall arrest must support at least how much per attached worker?
questions.why: Current OSHA rules require 5,000 lb per employee attached; the 5,400 lb figure came from a superseded lifeline rule.

questions.q: How wide must driveways between and around outdoor combustible storage piles be?
questions.why: OSHA requires driveways at least 15 ft wide, kept clear, forming grid units no larger than 50 x 150 ft.

questions.q: A stairway or ladder is required at a personnel access point when the break in elevation is at least:
questions.why: Breaks in elevation of 19 in or more need a stairway or ladder unless a ramp, runway, embankment or hoist is provided.

questions.q: Besides daily inspections, when must a competent person re-inspect an open excavation?
c: Only at the start of each work week
After every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event
Only when the depth exceeds 20 ft
Only after an OSHA compliance visit
questions.why: Excavations must be inspected daily and again after rainstorms or any occurrence that increases the hazard.

questions.q: An employer must have a written emergency action plan once it has at least how many employees?
questions.why: Employers with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally, so a written plan is required at 11 or more.

questions.q: What minimum clearance to combustible material must be kept at the sides of a temporary radiant-type heater?
questions.why: Radiant room heaters need 36 in of side clearance; circulating types need only 12 in.

questions.q: What Medicare tax rate is withheld from an employee's wages up to $200,000 in a year?
questions.why: The employee pays 1.45% and the employer matches it; 2.9% is the combined total and 0.9% is the additional tax above $200,000.

questions.q: How must a corporation with a sizable quarterly liability make its federal payroll tax deposits?
c: Mail a check with a Form 8109 coupon
Pay in cash at a local IRS office
Attach the payment to Form W-3
Electronic funds transfer, such as EFTPS
questions.why: Paper deposit coupons ended in 2011; all federal tax deposits must be made electronically.

questions.q: An employer is a monthly depositor if its employment taxes in the lookback period totaled:
questions.why: $50,000 or less in the lookback period means monthly deposits; more than that means semiweekly.

questions.q: What failure-to-deposit penalty applies to a payroll tax deposit made more than 15 days late (before an IRS notice)?
questions.why: The tiers are 2% (1-5 days), 5% (6-15 days), 10% (over 15 days) and 15% after an unpaid notice.

questions.q: When accumulated FUTA liability passes $500 at the end of a calendar quarter, when is the deposit due?
c: The last day of the month after the quarter ends
questions.why: FUTA over $500 is deposited by the end of the month following the quarter; Form 940 is filed annually.

questions.q: On a $5.1 million federal construction contract, the Miller Act payment bond normally must be:
questions.why: Since 1999 the payment bond equals 100% of the contract price unless the contracting officer finds that impractical.

questions.q: Which bond guarantees that a bidder, if awarded the job, will sign the contract and furnish the required bonds?
questions.why: A bid bond protects the owner if the selected bidder refuses to enter the contract or provide bonds.

questions.q: Which gross receipts limit determines whether a small contractor may use the completed-contract method for tax purposes?
questions.why: The TCJA raised the limit from $10 million to $25 million indexed ($31 million for 2025), based on the prior 3-year average.

questions.q: By what date must a contractor give subcontractors their copies of Form 1099-NEC?
questions.why: Form 1099-NEC is due to recipients (and to the IRS) by January 31.

questions.q: Which business may use the owner's SSN instead of obtaining an EIN?
c: A single-member LLC with three employees
A sole proprietorship with no employees and no excise or pension filings
questions.why: Sole proprietors and single-member LLCs need an EIN once they have employees; corporations and partnerships always need one.

questions.q: A non-exempt employee works 3 hours of overtime without the required supervisor approval. What must the employer do?
c: Refuse to pay for the unauthorized hours
Pay the hours at the overtime rate, and may discipline the employee
Pay the hours at straight time only
Convert the hours to unpaid comp time
questions.why: Work the employer suffers or permits must be paid; policy violations are handled by discipline, not by withholding wages.

questions.q: A federal NPDES stormwater permit is required for construction activity that disturbs at least:
questions.why: Disturbing 1 acre or more, or less if part of a larger common plan of 1 acre or more, triggers permit coverage.

questions.q: Manual fire alarm boxes must be located no more than what distance from the entrance to each exit?
questions.why: Pull stations go within 5 ft of each exit entrance, mounted 42-48 in above the floor.

questions.q: When fully open, a door in the means of egress may reduce the required egress width by no more than:
questions.why: A fully opened door may project at most 7 in into the required width, and no more than half at any position.

questions.q: An unsurcharged landscape retaining wall is exempt from a building permit if its height, from bottom of footing to top of wall, does not exceed:
questions.why: Walls over 4 ft, or any wall supporting a surcharge or impounding flammable liquids, need a permit.

questions.q: A building under construction will be 48 ft tall and is 20 ft from the lot line. What pedestrian protection is required?
c: A barrier and a covered walkway
questions.why: 20 ft falls between 1/4 (12 ft) and 1/2 (24 ft) of the height, which requires a barrier.

questions.q: What are the minimum size requirements for an enclosed fire service access elevator lobby?
questions.why: The lobby must be at least 150 sq ft with no dimension under 8 ft so firefighters can stage.

questions.q: Where ramp handrails are not continuous between runs, how far must they extend horizontally beyond the top and bottom of each run?
questions.why: Ramp handrail extensions must be at least 12 in at both the top and the bottom.

questions.q: What is the maximum live-load deflection allowed for a floor member?
questions.why: Floor members are limited to L/360 under live load; L/240 applies to total load.

questions.q: Footings must be stepped when the bottom surface slopes more than:
questions.why: A footing bottom sloping more than 10% must be stepped to keep bearing surfaces level.

questions.q: A notch at the end of a solid sawn floor joist may not exceed what portion of the joist depth?
questions.why: End notches are limited to 1/4 of the depth; notches elsewhere are limited to 1/6.

questions.q: At what maximum spacing must drip edge be mechanically fastened to the roof deck?
questions.why: Drip edge is fastened no more than 12 in apart, with 2 in laps and 2 in onto the deck.

questions.q: How is drip edge layered with underlayment on a shingle roof?
c: Over the underlayment at both eaves and rakes
Under the underlayment at eaves and over it at rakes
Under the underlayment at both eaves and rakes
Over the underlayment at eaves and under it at rakes
questions.why: At eaves the underlayment laps over the drip edge to shed water; at rakes the drip edge goes on top.

questions.q: Corner guards protecting fireproofing on columns exposed to forklift traffic must extend at least how high above the finished floor?
questions.why: Impact protection must reach at least 5 ft above the floor, or higher if needed for full protection.

questions.q: A masonry chimney must extend at least how far above the highest point where it passes through the roof?
questions.why: The 3-2-10 rule: 3 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above anything within 10 ft.

questions.q: A non-circular Type I handrail must have a perimeter dimension within what range?
questions.why: Non-circular Type I rails need a 4 to 6-1/4 in perimeter and a cross section of no more than 2-1/4 in.

questions.q: A pile standing unbraced in water may be considered laterally supported at what depth into stiff soil?
questions.why: Lateral support may be assumed 5 ft into stiff soil or 10 ft into soft soil.

questions.q: What minimum illumination is required at the walking surface of a means of egress while the building is occupied?
questions.why: Egress paths need at least 1 footcandle (11 lux) at the floor.

questions.q: During construction, a temporary or permanent stairway is required once the building rises more than what height above the lowest fire department vehicle access?
questions.why: Above 40 ft, a stair must be provided and kept within one floor of the highest secured deck.

questions.q: Regardless of airport proximity, FAA notice is required for a crane or structure taller than what height above ground level?
questions.why: Anything over 200 ft AGL needs Form 7460-1; closer to airports, imaginary-surface slopes set lower trigger heights.

questions.q: What is the minimum size, in the smallest dimension, of an accessible elevator car control button?
questions.why: Car and hall call buttons must be at least 3/4 in in their smallest dimension.

questions.q: When accessible parking spaces are striped, where is their width measured?
c: From the inside edge of each line
From the outside edge of each line
From the centerline of the markings
questions.why: Space and access aisle widths are measured to the centerline of the striping.

questions.q: A 50,000 lb load hangs from a two-leg bridle with each leg at 45 degrees from horizontal. About how much tension is in each leg?
questions.why: Each leg carries (W/2)/sin 45 = 0.707 x 50,000, about 35,400 lb; flatter angles raise leg tension.

questions.q: Which of the following may NOT be used as a grounding electrode?
c: 20 ft of 1/2 in rebar encased in a footing
Metal underground water pipe with 10 ft in contact with earth
A ground ring of 2 AWG bare copper
questions.why: Gas piping and aluminum are prohibited electrodes; concrete-encased rebar is permitted.

questions.q: Under the IPC, what is the maximum horizontal support spacing for PVC pipe?
questions.why: PVC and ABS are supported every 4 ft; small CPVC is 3 ft and PEX 32 in.

questions.q: What minimum STC rating is required for walls separating dwelling units when tested in a lab?
questions.why: Dwelling and sleeping unit separations need STC 50 (45 if field tested).

questions.q: How many studs does a 12 ft straight partition need at 16 in on center, ignoring corners, openings and waste?
questions.why: 144 in / 16 in = 9 spaces, plus 1 for the end stud, gives 10 studs.

questions.q: A trench is 18 ft wide at the top, 5 ft wide at the bottom, 8 ft deep and 750 ft long. How much material is removed?
questions.why: Average width (18+5)/2 = 11.5 ft x 8 ft x 750 ft = 69,000 cu ft.

questions.q: What color marking identifies Type L copper water tube?
questions.why: Type K is green, Type L blue and Type M red, from thickest to thinnest wall.

questions.q: What is the maximum threshold height for a sliding door serving a dwelling unit?
questions.why: Dwelling-unit sliding doors may have 3/4 in thresholds; other doors are limited to 1/2 in.

questions.q: Untreated wood siding must be kept at least how far above the ground?
questions.why: Wood within 6 in of earth, or within 2 in of exposed concrete, must be decay resistant or treated.

questions.q: A building has a 1,600 sq ft basement with no sprinklers. Exterior openings intended to avoid the sprinkler requirement must each have a minimum dimension of at least:
questions.why: Qualifying fire department access openings must be at least 30 in in their least dimension.
